identity.scope: First noninteractive CLI slice using existing HOST/EXEC; no full Agent platform

recommendation: First validate a benign local noninteractive fixture through the existing HOST/EXEC seam. Then validate one explicitly selected Claude Code installation, followed by a separate Codex compatibility case. Keep inbound MCP/report authority, interactive PTY and Agent-hosted product UI outside this first slice. Provider ordering is a proposal, not an approval or claim of current CLI support.

current_facts.fact: CliToolConfig contains only path and argv; source defaults are claude + [--print] and codex + [exec]. These are current repository defaults, NOT externally verified current provider interfaces.

CLI start_live passes configured path/args and request.project_root as cwd. Request task/fingerprint are required host metadata, but no task prompt, packet path, runId or report envelope is automatically added to child argv/stdin/environment.

StdProcess explicitly uses stdin=null, piped stdout/stderr, no PTY and no resize/permission-response input. It does not configure an isolated environment; ordinary OS child environment inheritance must not be presented as secret isolation.

ProcessPort has start/try_wait/cancel/try_read with independent stream Open/Eof/Error. Existing process slice waits for EOF and uses a first-observed-exit drain deadline. There is no general still-running child execution timeout in this port.
HOST owns accepted run/WORK lease and reconciles only terminal facts; provider Success does not accept/green a task. Local child exit is not an authenticated ReportRun submission.
Readonly .ess packet always remains NOT_READY without complete UI/approval authority. The shared report ingress schema and atomic/authenticated submission are proposals, not installed CLI ingestion.

first_slice_order_PROPOSED.gate: This decision and measurable fixture contract

first_slice_order_PROPOSED.work: Reuse existing ProcessPort/EXEC/host fixture capabilities to prove launch, argument token preservation, cwd, stdout/stderr, exit/EOF, cancellation and second-run exclusion. Direct benign executable only; no new provider abstraction.
first_slice_order_PROPOSED.gate: Executable fixture evidence; historical existing helper evidence may be cited but new envelope behavior is not considered tested yet

first_slice_order_PROPOSED.work: Lock exact packet/input delivery and captured-output binding for one run. Explicit configured argv can already name a fixture/input file; dynamic per-run packet injection is NOT currently implemented. Any required request/API change returns to architecture approval.
first_slice_order_PROPOSED.gate: No invented CLI prompt field or automatic stdin support

first_slice_order_PROPOSED.work: With user-named Claude Code path/version/argv/auth readiness and permitted task target, run a separate narrowly authorized compatibility check. Repeat as an independent Codex case using that installation's actual contract, not shared guessed flags.
first_slice_order_PROPOSED.gate: Both compatibility rows completed; each may be NOT RUN/BLOCKED independently

first_slice_order_PROPOSED.work: Only after separate Guard/document/ingress decisions: implementation-ready packet execution or authenticated report submission. Inbound MCP and both embedding directions remain separate workstreams.
first_slice_order_PROPOSED.gate: No first-slice authorization extends to those features

allowed_and_forbidden_PROPOSED.allowed: An explicit local benign executable using argv tokens and an explicit disposable bound cwd; controlled modes such as emit-output / nonzero-exit / await-cancel are fixture requirements, not existing provider commands. Existing start_run/poll_chunks/cancel_run and settings path/args are reused only within owner-selected scope. After separate approval, one exact provider executable/argv may be tested.
forbidden: No Agent launch, login, token read/write, provider version invocation or authentication change in this planning task.
No shell command string, cmd /c, PowerShell -Command, shell expansion, eval, arbitrary request-supplied executable or dynamically appended unreviewed args in the proposed first envelope.
No broad auto-approve/permission-bypass flags, unknown network endpoint probing, automatic package install/update, persistent daemon/session, stdin dialogue or PTY fallback.
No task/report metadata accepted as authorization; no child output promoted into SPEC/GUARD authority or product acceptance.
No schema/Port/DTO/Manager/framework/dependency changes to fit a guessed provider interface.
allowed_and_forbidden_PROPOSED.scope_honesty: The existing ProcessPort is a low-level launcher, not a security allowlist or sandbox. These are proposed envelope restrictions that need a selected enforcement/fixture boundary; do not advertise that current executable/argv settings prevent arbitrary child actions.

input_output_contract_PROPOSED.input: Explicit selected executable + exact ordered argv vector + HOST-bound project_root/work_item_id/current fingerprint. Empty/invalid/unapproved path rejects under existing gates. No implicit PATH executable discovery or new secret-bearing args proposed; exact path policy to be approved for real installation.
input_output_contract_PROPOSED.source: If a module packet is supplied, bind its explicit source-relative path, exact .ess SHA256, moduleId/taskId, packet payload SHA256 and current project/worktree snapshot. Recheck freshness before handoff; no external UI discovery or XML repair. A NOT_READY packet can be inspected but cannot authorize implementation.
input_output_contract_PROPOSED.delivery_choice: For first fixture, use an explicit already-supported argv token naming a disposable read-only input file or literal fixture string. No new child stdin or request prompt field. For actual provider, whether input is argv/file/stdin and size/quoting/encoding limits are UNKNOWN until exact installed interface and user target are provided; unsupported required stdin => ARCHITECTURE_GAP, not silent port extension.
input_output_contract_PROPOSED.output: Capture stdout/stderr as existing text chunks with per-stream ordering; preserve existing lossy-UTF8 contract. First fixture emits fixed marker + known payload for exact assertions. Actual provider structured-output schema and permission/auth notifications are UNKNOWN; malformed/empty output is not accepted report evidence merely because exit0.
input_output_contract_PROPOSED.exit: Reuse existing exit classification and terminal-once after captured chunks. 0 means provider process success only, nonzero failure, cancellation as existing direct-child intent. No product green/acceptance. Plain wait-only error recovery remains existing follow-up, not fixed by this envelope.
input_output_contract_PROPOSED.cancel: Existing request-ack + continuing poll/drain, direct-child-only cancellation. Fixed2,000ms is an observed-post-exit drain check, not whole task runtime timeout. Both EOF at an observation can complete even if caller waited longer; otherwise open streams at elapsed>=2,000ms fail incomplete. Unbounded buffers and inherited-reader lifetime remain explicit limitations.
input_output_contract_PROPOSED.runtime_timeout: UNKNOWN for real provider and not added by this plan. Fixture harness may use a bounded test deadline solely to classify environment/harness failure; it must not be reported as production cancellation/timeout proof.
input_output_contract_PROPOSED.reports: HOST associates captured process observations with its accepted run/task/project/fingerprint and selected source packet hashes. Child-returned runId/taskId/PASS are untrusted claimed data. Report files may be reviewed as artifacts, but authenticated ReportRun/claim/lease/report_id/sequence/CAS semantics stay in the separately unapproved ingress proposal; no new acceptance grant is invented.
input_output_contract_PROPOSED.failure: Invalid/missing config, stale source or unapproved scope rejects before launch where enforcement exists; missing producer/input/report schema is NOT_READY. No automatic retry or interactive/login fallback. Auth-needed provider behavior must be detected according to verified installed interface; no guessed error-string classifier.

architecture.domain_application: Existing run/WORK lease and acceptance rules; HOST orchestrates accepted starts. No domain owns provider flags or authentication.
architecture.ports_adapters: Existing AgentPort and ProcessPort; CliAgentAdapter config mapping and StdProcess OS adapter. UI commands are driving adapters. No new protocol/session interface.
architecture.ownership_mutation: HOST/WORK own run/task/project/lease. EXEC owns output/terminal projection. Child is untrusted. First planning slice mutates none. Future fixture artifact/output files are isolated test data, not new SSOT.
architecture.transactions: Preserve existing preflight/start/lease and terminal reconciliation; source snapshot check is a handoff freshness check, not an OS write-isolation guarantee. New report commit transaction is excluded.
architecture.forbidden_dependencies: UI directly spawning provider; Domain depending on CLI SDK/FS; Agent writing board/SPEC directly; report ingestion bypassing HOST; interpreting process success as approval.

diagram_A:
Existing desktop command [driving]
 -> HOST start_run / approved start_implementation [application; latter authority still a separate gap]
 -> AgentPort -> CliAgentAdapter -> ProcessPort
 <- StdProcess [driven OS adapter] -> explicit noninteractive child
 -> stdout/stderr/status -> EXEC chunks/terminal -> HOST WORK reconciliation -> UI
No stdin/PTY/native provider session or Agent network added.
diagram_B:
Settings(path,argv) -> CliAgentAdapter
StartRunRequest(project,task,fingerprint) -> HOST/EXEC binding; project supplies childcwd
Explicit sourcepacket manifest -- proposed approved handoff --> configured child input
Child output -> host-bound capture artifact -> human/evidence review
Future ReportRun ingress [NOT IMPLEMENTED] remains separate; no direct child->accept/green route.

acceptance_PROPOSED: AC1: Owner approves benignfixture-first and exact executable/argv/input/output/cwd scope; no provider launch inferred.
AC2: Real Claude Code and Codex rows each name exact version/path/argv/auth readiness/allowed target and receive independent PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED/NOT RUN.
AC3: Existing HOST/EXEC/ProcessPort remain; no stdin/PTY/Manager/dependency/DTO extension hidden in implementation.
AC4: Source/packet/task/worktree binding is explicit; NOT_READY packet never grants implementation authority.
AC5: Output/exit/cancel/duplicate-run behavior respects existing module contract; no process success -> acceptance or fake real-provider proof.
AC6: Unknown input/output/runtime/permission details remain unresolved until chosen; no guessed defaults or secret reads.
AC7: Before any formal Skeleton/RED, approve affected contracts/UI schema/file scope; current packet is planning only.
cost_and_non_goals: Planning cost: zero production files, types, dependencies or new interfaces. Proposed first fixture should reuse existing test seams; exact test/helper file count chosen only after envelope approval. No shared provider platform, inbound MCP, report store, PTY/session persistence, login manager or automatic permissions.
